items.item_text: A bachelor's degree (*attach transcript) from an accredited institution; AND

Two (2) years of increasingly responsible experience coordinating or providing instructional and non-instructional services to adults in a learning center environment, preferably in a community college; OR
An equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience.
Methods, practices, terminology, and procedures involved in the operation of the library and learning resources centers.
Schedule, coordinate, and chair meetings.
Library terminology, practices, procedures, and systems, including acquisition, processing, cataloging, circulation, and automation.
Manage conflict between individuals and group members to bring to joint consensus.
Principles and practices of supervision and training.
Analyze fiscal information to develop and maintain budgets.
Office procedures, methods, and equipment.
Plan and organize work to meet changing priorities and deadlines.
Office productivity computer applications including word processing, spreadsheet, email, and database applications.
Understand and carry out oral and written directions.
Library and learning resources-related software and equipment including automation and instructional software.
Exercise initiative and independence of judgment and action.
Principles and procedures of inventory and records management.
Research solutions to problems and new tasks.
Basic mathematical principles.
Prepare reports by gathering and organizing data from a variety of sources.
Basic principles of business letter writing and report preparation.
Customer service and public relations methods and techniques.
Principles of program planning and program review.
Learn and apply new information and skills.
Communicate effectively, both orally and in writing.
Maintains current knowledge of methods and technologies pertinent to the project(s); conduct, and review research studies, and surveys regarding project constituents, clients, and trends.

Demonstrate sensitivity to and understanding of the diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, and ethnic backgrounds of community college students, faculty, and staff.
